purpose: Independent common-move explanation drafts covering preserved references and appended expansion variants.
authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
reference_scope: Drafting used existing names, aliases, and structural fields, not the earlier catalog descriptions or the private reference guide. One narrow technical fact check for Electric Kicks is identified separately below. Common movement identities and historical provenance are not claimed as newly invented.
mechanics_policy: This file changes no catalog identity, alias, count, rotation, foot state, or weight-change field. Teaching variants and ambiguity flags require separate instructor and mechanics review before adoption.

entries.name: Balance
entries.explanation: Balance is the ability to stay steady while standing, stepping, or turning. If a dance uses “balance” as the name of a step sequence, that sequence needs its own instructions.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm whether this entry teaches general balance or names a particular balance-step pattern.

entries.name: Ball
entries.explanation: The ball of the foot is the padded area just behind the toes. Placing weight there is different from standing on the tips of your toes.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Beats
entries.explanation: A beat is a regular pulse you can hear or feel in the music. Dancers use those pulses to place their movements in time.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Bpm
entries.explanation: BPM means beats per minute and describes how fast the music's pulse moves. A higher BPM means more beats happen each minute.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Break
entries.explanation: A break step usually checks or changes the direction of movement through a weight change. The dance must specify the stepping foot, direction, and what follows; “break” can also describe a change or pause in the music.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm whether “break” means a checking step, a musical break, or a choreographic interruption.

entries.name: Bridge
entries.explanation: A bridge is a connecting or contrasting section of music or choreography. In a dance, its movements, length, and placement must be explained.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm the glossary's intended distinction between a bridge and a tag.

entries.name: Cha Cha
entries.explanation: Cha cha can describe a musical style, dance style, or a step rhythm with a quick group of weight changes. The name alone does not specify the feet, direction, or timing of a particular sequence.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm whether the entry concerns cha cha music, styling, rhythm, or a specific step pattern.

entries.name: Clockwise
entries.explanation: Clockwise means turning in the same direction as the hands of a clock. Imagine looking down at the dancer from above.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Count
entries.explanation: A count is a spoken or written timing marker that helps you match movements to music. The dance instructions show what happens on each numbered count or subdivision.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Count "&"
entries.explanation: An “&” count marks a timing point between numbered counts. It commonly sits halfway between them, but the intended rhythm should make its placement clear.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm the intended subdivision when the rhythm is uneven or swung.

entries.name: Counter Clockwise
entries.explanation: Counterclockwise, also called anticlockwise, means turning opposite to the hands of a clock. Imagine looking down at the dancer from above.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Diagonal
entries.explanation: Diagonal means moving or facing at a slant between straight ahead, sideways, or backward directions. The instructions should identify which diagonal and whether it refers to your body or the room.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Specify whether diagonals use the dancer's current facing or fixed room directions.

entries.name: Forward
entries.explanation: Forward usually means toward the direction your body is facing. A dance may instead use a fixed room direction, so follow its stated reference.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Home
entries.explanation: Home means a reference position that the dancer returns to. The dance must establish whether this means a foot position, body position, or place on the floor.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Define the home position within the dance.

entries.name: Phrased
entries.explanation: A phrased dance is organized into named or lettered sections that follow a stated order. Those sections can repeat or change order to match the music.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Restart
entries.explanation: A restart means beginning the dance again before completing the usual sequence. The instructions identify where this happens and any adjustment needed to begin again.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Rhythm
entries.explanation: Rhythm is the pattern of timing and emphasis in music or movement. It includes how long actions last and where the stronger accents fall.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Spot Dance
entries.explanation: A spot dance stays within a relatively small area instead of continually traveling around the floor. It can still include steps in different directions and turns.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Stationary Turn
entries.explanation: A stationary turn changes your facing while keeping you in roughly the same place. The turn amount, direction, footwork, and timing must be specified separately.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Syncopation
entries.explanation: Syncopation places movement or emphasis between, or across, the main beats. The dance instructions show exactly where those actions fall.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Tag
entries.explanation: A tag is an extra section added at a specified point in the dance. Its movements, length, and location must be given so you know when to add it.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Tempo
entries.explanation: Tempo is the speed of the music's underlying pulse. It describes how fast the beat moves, rather than how many steps you take.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Turn
entries.explanation: A turn changes the direction your body faces. Its direction, amount, timing, and supporting footwork need separate instructions.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Turn In
entries.explanation: Turn in means rotate a body part or change your facing inward relative to a stated reference. Specify what turns, what inward means here, and the amount of rotation.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Define the inward reference before teaching the turn.

entries.name: Turn Out
entries.explanation: Turn out means rotate a body part or change your facing outward relative to a stated reference. Specify what turns, what outward means here, and the amount of rotation.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Define the outward reference before teaching the turn.

entries.name: Waltz
entries.explanation: Waltz can describe music with a repeating three-beat grouping or a dance style associated with that music. The label does not specify a particular step sequence, direction, or turn.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm whether the entry concerns waltz music, styling, or a particular step pattern.

entries.name: Across
entries.explanation: Step across the front of the other leg and transfer weight to the crossing foot. Specify which foot leads and how far it crosses.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Ball Change
entries.explanation: Take weight briefly onto the ball of one foot, then transfer weight to the other foot. State the foot placements and rhythm so the two changes fit the intended count.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Behind
entries.explanation: Step behind the other leg and transfer weight to the crossing foot. Keep the crossing distance suited to the next step.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Brush
entries.explanation: Swing the free foot so its ball lightly brushes the floor, then continues onward without taking weight. Specify the direction of the swing.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Chug
entries.explanation: Make a small forward movement on the supporting foot while keeping the other foot free. The dance should specify the free-leg position and whether the supporting foot slides or briefly leaves the floor.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm whether chug uses a slide or hop and specify the free-leg action.

entries.name: Cross
entries.explanation: Step across the line of the other leg and take weight on that foot. The instructions must say whether the crossing is in front or behind.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Cross Kick
entries.explanation: Extend the free leg into a kick across the front of the body. Keep your weight on the supporting foot and use the stated kick height and direction.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Diagonal Kick
entries.explanation: Kick the free foot toward the stated diagonal without transferring weight. Specify whether that diagonal is measured from the body or a fixed wall.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Dig
entries.explanation: Place the indicated part of the free foot on the floor as a firm accent without transferring weight. Specify whether this is a heel dig or another contact, and where the foot goes.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Dig requires an explicit heel or other contact; the name alone is not a unique foot instruction.

entries.name: Drag
entries.explanation: Draw the free foot along the floor toward the supporting foot or another stated position. This entry finishes without transferring weight to the moving foot.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Draw is shared by Drag and Slide, whose recorded weight changes are zero and one. Do not merge them by alias.

entries.name: Fan
entries.explanation: Keep one part of a foot in contact with the floor while swinging the other part outward and back. Specify whether the heel or toes move and which foot performs the action.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Flare
entries.explanation: Flare is a label that needs a specific foot or leg action before it can be followed. State the moving contact or body part, its path, and the finish without assuming a full-leg swing or a particular fan variation.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: The name does not establish a unique leg path or finishing position.

entries.name: Flick
entries.explanation: Bend the free knee to send the foot into a quick lifted accent, commonly behind or beside the body. State the direction and return position without transferring weight to that foot.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Heel Bounce
entries.explanation: Raise and lower the indicated heel or heels while keeping the front of the foot on the floor. Specify the number of bounces and which foot carries the weight.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Heel Clicks
entries.explanation: Bring the heels together to make the stated clicking accent. Specify the starting foot position, supporting contacts, and whether the action stays grounded or leaves the floor.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Starting support and heel-click technique need confirmation; do not infer a jump from the label.

entries.name: Heel Fan
entries.explanation: Keep the toes in place while moving the heel outward and back. Use the named foot and keep the weight arrangement specified for the dance.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Heel Twist
entries.explanation: Rotate the heels toward the stated side while the front of the feet provides the contact with the floor. The dance must give the return action and whether one or both heels move.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Hitch
entries.explanation: Lift the free knee while keeping weight on the supporting leg. State the knee direction and the position needed for the next action.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Hold
entries.explanation: Wait for the stated count or counts without taking another step. Keep the current weight placement unless an additional styling instruction says otherwise.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Hook
entries.explanation: Bend the free knee and bring that foot across the supporting leg in the specified hook position. Keep it unweighted and distinguish a front hook from any behind-the-leg variation.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Hop
entries.explanation: Leave the floor briefly from one foot and land on that same foot. Specify any travel or turn separately.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Jumping Jacks
entries.explanation: Jump to an open foot position, then jump back toward a closed position. The dance must specify the landing support, spacing, and any arm action.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Landing support is unspecified in the structural record.

entries.name: Kick
entries.explanation: Extend the free leg into a kick in the stated direction, keeping weight on the other foot. Use the height and return position called for by the dance.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Knee Pops
entries.explanation: Make a small knee accent by bending and releasing the indicated knee, allowing the heel action needed for that movement. The dance must identify the knee and support position; this entry does not add a weight transfer.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Leap
entries.explanation: Push off one foot and land on the other foot with a brief airborne phase between them. Specify the travel direction and landing position.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Louie Louis
entries.explanation: This name needs a demonstrated foot-and-heel sequence before it can be followed reliably. The recorded variation lasts two counts without changing weight, so its starting position, heel actions, and ending position must be supplied.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Rare label: a reliable step sequence was not inferred from the name and mechanics alone.

entries.name: Lunge
entries.explanation: Step into the stated side direction and take weight onto that leg while bending its knee. Use a comfortable distance and specify how the dancer returns or continues.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Mashed Potatoes
entries.explanation: Mashed potatoes names a family of swiveling footwork variations rather than one universal sequence. Specify the heel and toe actions, travel, and support; a variation that changes weight needs different weight-change data from this entry.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: The record has zero weight changes; weight-changing mashed-potatoes variations need separate mechanics.

entries.name: Pigeon Toed
entries.explanation: Use alternating inward and outward angles of the feet to make the specified sideways movement. The dance must explain which heels or toes pivot and how the feet are supported throughout.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm the exact contact pattern and how the zero recorded weight changes fit the traveling variation.

entries.name: Point
entries.explanation: Extend the free foot to the stated position and touch the toe to the floor without taking weight. Keep it available for the next action.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Press
entries.explanation: Place the free foot forward and apply the stated pressure while the same foot remains the primary support. If the movement fully transfers weight, record that as a different variation.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Clarify partial pressure versus a full transfer; this record has zero weight changes.

entries.name: Recover
entries.explanation: Return weight to the foot that was supporting you before the preceding rock or similar action. Keep the feet placed as directed rather than automatically taking a new traveling step.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Ronde de Jambe
entries.explanation: Trace a curved path with the free leg around the supporting leg. Specify whether the toe stays near the floor or is lifted, and give the start, direction, and finish of the arc.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Scoot
entries.explanation: Make a small forward scooting movement on the supporting foot, keeping that same foot as the support. Specify the free-leg action; a step-and-hop skip is a separate weight-changing variation.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: The Skip alias can imply different step-and-hop weight transfers from this zero-transfer scoot.

entries.name: Scuff
entries.explanation: Swing the free foot so its heel briefly grazes the floor and continues forward. Keep the foot unweighted after the scuff unless a following instruction places it down.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Slap
entries.explanation: Use a hand to make the stated slapping accent, such as contacting the thigh or the raised foot. Specify the hand, target, and timing while maintaining the required support.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Slide
entries.explanation: Move a foot smoothly along the floor to the stated position and take weight on it. This weighted slide differs from drawing an unweighted foot toward the support foot.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Draw is shared by Drag and Slide, whose recorded weight changes are zero and one. Do not merge them by alias.

entries.name: Splits
entries.explanation: Open the indicated heels or toes apart, then bring them back as directed. Specify which part of each foot stays in contact with the floor; this is foot swiveling rather than a full-leg split.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Stamp
entries.explanation: Strike the floor with the indicated foot as an accent and leave it unweighted. Make the intended support clear because some dances use stamp and stomp differently.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Stamp and stomp vocabulary varies; this entry is explicitly unweighted.

entries.name: Step
entries.explanation: Place a foot in the stated direction and transfer weight onto it. Specify the distance and facing when those affect the next movement.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Stomp
entries.explanation: Place the indicated foot firmly on the floor and take weight on it. This record is a weighted stomp; an unweighted stomp-up must be identified and recorded separately.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Stomp up alias implies an unweighted variation, but the record has one weight change.

entries.name: Stride
entries.explanation: Take a traveling step of the length stated in the dance and transfer weight onto that foot. Keep the distance comfortable and specify the travel direction.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Sweep
entries.explanation: Move the free foot through a smooth arc around the supporting foot without transferring weight. State the start and finish positions and whether the toe stays on the floor.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Swivel
entries.explanation: Rotate the specified heels, toes, or feet toward a side using the stated contact points. Give the order, return action, and support position; swivel alone does not define one fixed sequence.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Swivet
entries.explanation: Pivot one foot through its heel contact while the other pivots through the ball or front of the foot. Specify the side, weight placement, and any return action before beginning this coordinated foot action.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Instructor review must confirm heel/toe support and return sequence.

entries.name: Toe Fan
entries.explanation: Keep the heel in place while opening the toes outward, then return the toes as directed. Specify the foot and how the weight is supported.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Together
entries.explanation: Bring the free foot beside the supporting foot and transfer weight to it. A touch beside the other foot is different because it does not take weight.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Together can mean the single closing transfer or the two-count Step Together sequence. Do not collapse these entries through the shared alias.

entries.name: Touch
entries.explanation: Contact the floor lightly with the indicated part of the free foot without taking weight. Specify where the touch goes and leave that foot free for the next action.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Walk
entries.explanation: Take a walking step in the stated direction and transfer weight onto the moving foot. Use the pace and step length required by the dance.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Weight Change
entries.explanation: Move your weight from the current supporting foot to the other foot. The feet may stay in place or move as separately instructed.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Ankle Rock
entries.explanation: An ankle rock needs instructions for the foot positions and rocking action. This version uses two weight changes over two counts and finishes facing the starting direction.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: The name and structural data do not establish the ankle-rock mechanics.

entries.name: Balance ½ Turn
entries.explanation: This balance-turn sequence uses three weight-changing steps over three counts and finishes a half turn. The starting foot, step directions, and placement of the turn must be specified.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: The exact catalog label has encoding damage: the supplied label is “Balance replacement-character Turn,” with alias “Balance Half Turn.” Preserve that issue for correction rather than silently guessing the damaged character.

entries.name: Balance Step
entries.explanation: This balance step uses three weight-changing steps over three counts and finishes with no net turn. The name alone does not establish the step directions or foot placements.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Balance step is not sufficiently specific to establish a unique three-step pattern.

entries.name: Boogie Walk
entries.explanation: A boogie walk is a stylized walking sequence. This version uses three weight changes over three counts with no net turn; the walking direction and intended knee, leg, or body styling need explanation.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm the intended equivalence of Boogie Walk and Camel Walk and specify the styling.

entries.name: Box Step
entries.explanation: A box step arranges movement around a box-shaped floor pattern. This version records three weight changes across four counts with no net turn, so the exact step order and action without a weight transfer must be specified.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: The recorded three weight changes across four counts require an explicit unweighted action or hold; do not substitute a four-transfer box automatically.

entries.name: Break Turn
entries.explanation: This is a two-count turning sequence with two weight changes. The starting foot, turn direction, turn amount, and placement of the weight transfers must be supplied.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: The aliases do not establish one universal turn amount or direction. Both remain unspecified.

entries.name: Charleston
entries.explanation: A Charleston sequence combines stepping with unweighted foot actions, such as kicks or touches. This version takes four counts, changes weight twice, and has no net turn; the exact order and directions must be given.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Specify whether the unweighted actions are kicks, points, touches, or a combination.

entries.name: Coaster Step
entries.explanation: A coaster step moves back, brings the feet together, then steps forward. This version fits three weight changes into two counts without a turn; the starting foot and timing must be stated.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Cross & Unwind
entries.explanation: Cross a foot as directed, then unwind to finish a half turn from the starting facing. This two-count version records two weight changes, so the crossing position and weight transfer during the unwind need explicit instructions.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Confirm where the second weight change occurs and which foot supports the finish; unwind instructions can otherwise leave weight unclear.

entries.name: Cross Rock
entries.explanation: Rock onto a crossed step, then recover weight to the other foot. This version uses two counts and two weight changes without a turn; the starting foot and crossing position must be specified.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Cross Shuffle
entries.explanation: A cross shuffle combines a crossing step, a side step, and another crossing step. This version fits three weight changes into two counts without a turn; the starting foot, crossing position, and timing must be stated.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Electric Kicks
entries.explanation: Alternate a forward rock and recovery with a backward rock and recovery while adding a kick by the free leg on each action. Specify each kick direction and keep the four weight changes clear; confirm this electric-kicks variation with an instructor.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Mechanical sequence independently drafted after a narrow fact check against an instructor-authored glossary. Confirm kick directions and the intended four-transfer variation.

entries.name: Extended Grapevine
entries.explanation: An extended grapevine lengthens the sideways travel through side and crossing steps. This version has no net turn, but its length, crossing order, weight changes, and ending action must be specified.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Duration and weight changes are unspecified; “extended” does not establish a particular length.

entries.name: Grapevine
entries.explanation: A grapevine travels sideways through side and crossing steps. This four-count version has three weight changes and no net turn; the instructions must identify the crossing position and the action that does not transfer weight.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Grapevine 1/4 Turn
entries.explanation: This grapevine combines sideways travel and crossing steps with a quarter turn. It uses four counts and three weight changes; the instructions must locate the turn and identify the action without a weight transfer.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Heel Ball Change
entries.explanation: Make an unweighted heel touch, take weight onto the ball of that foot, then change weight to the other foot. This version fits the actions into two counts with two weight changes and no net turn; foot placements and timing must be stated.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Heel Ball Cross
entries.explanation: Make an unweighted heel touch, take weight onto the ball of that foot, then cross the other foot with weight. This version takes two counts and has two weight changes without a turn; the heel placement, crossing position, and timing must be specified.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Heel Ball Cross records two weight changes but changes foot_start R to foot_end L. Confirm the field convention and intended ending support before using this as a validated transition.

entries.name: Heel Grind
entries.explanation: Place weight onto a heel and rotate the foot around that heel, then transfer weight as directed. This version takes two counts with two weight changes and no net turn; the swivel direction and exit step must be specified.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.

entries.name: Heel Jack
entries.explanation: A heel jack combines a heel presentation with accompanying steps. This entry records four counts, two weight changes, and no net turn, so the full step order, heel placement, and unweighted actions must be supplied.
entries.authorship_note: New explanation draft written for this project; not a copyright certification or instructor approval.
review_notes: Heel jack has insufficient sequencing information here to teach a specific four-count, two-transfer variant.

entries.name: Heel Pivot

review_findings.note: The existing name contains U+FFFD. Its half-turn alias and 180-degree field agree, but the name is preserved exactly for a separate reviewed correction.
Draw is shared by Drag and Slide, whose recorded weight changes are zero and one. Do not merge them by alias.
The Stomp record has one weight change while its Stomp up alias can mean an unweighted action. Keep the weighted explanation explicit and review the alias.
Heel Ball Cross records two weight changes but changes foot_start R to foot_end L. Confirm the field convention and intended ending support before using this as a validated transition.
Rolling vine and Rolling grapevine appear under both the 360-degree Rolling Full Turn and the 180-degree Vine with 1/2 turn. Preserve both identities and require explicit variation selection.
Mashed Potatoes records zero weight changes. A traveling variation with transfers must not inherit that value unchanged.
Scoot has zero weight changes; its Skip alias can describe a different step-and-hop pattern with transfers.
Box Step records four counts and three transfers, so a four-transfer box cannot be silently substituted.
The paddle-turn record has zero weight changes. Confirm continuing support and free-foot action rather than teaching alternating weighted steps.
The side-rock quarter-turn aliases name both left and right turns. The single signed numeric rotation cannot represent both simultaneously.
Sailor Step Turning is a broad name but the record defines one quarter-turn magnitude. Other turn amounts need separate mechanics.
Clap has foot_start='e'. A hand clap does not by itself establish a free or supporting foot.
Together can mean the single closing transfer or the two-count Step Together sequence. Do not collapse these entries through the shared alias.
Names and available structural fields do not establish complete teachable sequences for these variations. Each needs instructor-supplied details before being presented as a fixed pattern.
